correctness.rationale: Exactly two nonsquarefree factorization types occur for Ω(n)=3: p³ and p²q with distinct primes. For a cube τ²=16 and σ+φ=2p³+p+1; at odd p, 2p³≡2p mod16, hence p≡5 mod16; p=2 fails. For p²q, τ²=36 and σ+φ=q(2p²+1)+2p+1. The cases p=2,q=2 fail. If p=3 one gets q≡11 mod36. If odd p≠3, modulo3 forces p≡1 mod3, modulo4 forces q≡3 mod4, and modulo9 gives: p≡1 mod9 with q≡2 mod3; p≡4 mod9 with q=3; p≡7 mod9 impossible. All implications are reversible, giving exactly the three disjoint branches. Independent direct modular tests over 78 primes and 6006 ordered distinct prime pairs found zero discrepancies. The proof is entirely unbounded by its exhaustive residue split.
